# odyssey-016 — new rendering candidates (Odyssey 4.219–331)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| νηπενθές τ’ ἄχολόν τε (221, of Helen's drug) | "grief-easing and anger-easing" | "that eased grief and eased anger" | "nepenthe" (bare transliteration, not a translation), "sorrow-quelling", "wrath-calming", "banishing pain and anger" (loses the privative-compound structure of both words) |
| Πολύδαμνα, Θῶνος παράκοιτις (228, a named woman) | "Polydamna, Thon's consort" | "Polydamna, the wife of Thon" | "Thon's queen" (παράκοιτις is plain "bedfellow, wife", not a rank-title), embellishing either name as if their story were known |
| Παιήονός … γενέθλης (232, "of the race of Paieon") | "of the race of Paieon" | "descended from Paieon" | "Paean" (confuses the god Paieon with the epithet/hymn-name Paean), "Apollo" (a distinct, though related, healing god in Homer — flagged once at the note, not conflated), "the race of healers" (drops the proper name) |
| Ἄντικλος (4.286, proper name) | "Antiklos" | "Antiklos" | Latinizing to "Antiklus"; the name is a hapax, occurring nowhere else in the poem, so it carries no epithet to fix and is rendered as a plain transliteration |
| τανύπεπλος (4.305, of Helen) | "long-robed" | "long-robed" | "long-gowned", "trailing-robed" — a transparent compound (τανύ- "long, stretched" + πέπλος "robe"); fixed now as Helen's standing epithet since it is likely to recur with her elsewhere in the poem |

Note: καρτερὸς ἀνήρ (242, "the strong man") also recurs at 4.271 in the next paragraph (drafted in a different slice) but is left unfixed here per the task brief, which called it "plain, not yet fixed."
Note: θεοείκελος (4.276, of Deiphobus) reuses the wording already fixed in the house table for Telemachus at 3.416 ("god-resembling" / "who was like a god"), simply applied to a new referent — not a new rendering, so no new row.
